filed  by  the  sole  accused  in  crime  No.1662  of  2022 of  Sooranad  Police  Station, 
Kollam, 
registered under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC.

2.
The  prosecution  allegation  is  that, 
on  19.12.2022  at  7.00  a.m.,
 t h e   w i f e   o f   t h e   p e t i t i o n e r   w a s  found hanging in the bed room of her matrimonial home, 
and  she committed  suicide  due  to  the  physical  and  mental torture meted out to her by the petitioner. 
3. 
Heard  learned  counsel  for  the  petitioner  and  learned Public Prosecutor.
4. 
Learned  Public  Prosecutor  opposed  the  bail  application.
B.A.NO.623 OF 2024   3   
5. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that  the  victim, 
who  was  the  wife  of  the  petitioner, 
was  having some  mental  problems, 
for  which  he  had  taken  her  for  a counselling  on  03.08.2022. 
Moreover, 
the  deceased  Anija  Thampi  was having illicit connection with  a  relative  named  Syamkumar, 
and  she
was upset  when  the petitioner found out their illicit connection.
6.

f a t h e r  

w h i c h shows that the petitioner was a drunkard,
and he used to ill-treat her physically as well as mentally.
It is true that FIR was registered under Section 174 of IPC initially,
and after one and a half years,
Sections 498A and 306 of IPC  were i n c o r p o r a t e d i m p l i c a t i n g t h e p e t i t i o n e r h e r e i n .  7 .

So this Court is not inclined to release him  on pre-arrest bail. 
8.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 294(b), 323, 324 and 498A of IPC.
2. The prosecution case is that the accused being the husband of the defacto complainant subjected her to cruelty both physically and mentally on the ground of dowry, voluntarily caused hurt to her,
abused her in filthy words and thereby he alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3. According to the petitioner, the dispute has been amicably settled with the defacto complainant and that she had agreed to drop all further proceedings relating to the above dispute.
She has no further grievance against the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 5. The learned Public Prosecutor, after getting instruction from the investigating officer also submitted that the dispute has been amicably settled between the parties and that the victim is not at all interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
6. Considering the fact that the offence involved in this case is not heinous and very serious, but purely a matrimonial and private dispute, which has been amicably settled between the parties,
quashment of further proceedings is necessary for maintaining harmonious relationship between the parties.
7.
In the result, this Crl. M.C is allowed.
